question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Stimulus washout with chromatin and re-stimulation time course: After a defined AP-1-inducing stimulus, wash it out and track FOS/JUN occupancy (CUT&RUN), chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), and enhancer marks (H3K27ac) over days. Then re-stimulate and compare the speed and magnitude of target gene induction against naive cells, since faster or stronger re-induction without new AP-1 binding would indicate a memory.
2. Inducible degradation of AP-1 during and after a priming window: Use an auxin- or dTAG-degradable FOS or JUN allele to remove AP-1 at different times relative to a priming stimulus. Measure whether the memory-like transcriptional and chromatin state persists after AP-1 is gone, which separates AP-1 being required to establish memory from being required to maintain it.
3. Synthetic tethered AP-1 memory circuit at a reporter locus: Tether engineered AP-1 components (or a dimerized bZIP fusion) to a single-copy reporter with a dox-controlled recruiter, then turn the recruiter off and measure reporter expression, chromatin state, and H3K27ac/H3K4me1 over weeks. Persistence without the tether would show that AP-1 is sufficient to write a self-maintaining state, while mutating its DNA-binding domain would test necessity.
4. Live single-cell AP-1 reporter tracking across repeated pulses: Track AP-1 activity in individual cells with a live fluorescent reporter during repeated stimulus pulses of varying spacing and strength. Test whether prior pulse history predicts later response magnitude or timing (for example with mutual information or Markov models), and whether this history-dependence is lost when cells are imaged in heterogeneous or lineage-tracked populations.
5. Pulse-chase protein turnover versus persistence of memory: Use SNAP- or HaloTag-labelled FOS/JUN with pulse-chase labelling to measure AP-1 protein and DNA-bound half-lives in the same cells where memory persists. If memory lasts well beyond AP-1 turnover, combined with mutation of AP-1 motifs at memory-associated enhancers (base editing) and Micro-C or Hi-C for 3D contacts, this would point toward an epigenetic or 3D-architecture-based mechanism rather than a self-sustaining AP-1 feedback loop.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Quench-chase-pulse labelling of parental histones at memory enhancers
ideas.description: Use inducible SNAP- or Halo-tagged H3.3 to label nucleosomes present during priming, then quench and chase through one to several cell divisions and pulse new histones. Compare retention of parental versus newly deposited marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) at AP-1-bound memory enhancers, with sorted daughters, to test whether memory is inherited through recycled nucleosomes rather than through AP-1 itself.

ideas.title: Reversible S-phase block during the priming window
ideas.description: Prime cells with a defined AP-1 stimulus while holding them in G1 with a reversible CDK4/6 or CDC7 inhibitor, or in G2/M with a comparable block, then release and test re-induction. If memory is lost or diluted without DNA replication, it depends on replication-coupled chromatin dilution rather than on a stable, non-replicative state.

ideas.title: Signaling-layer memory via phosphatase levels, not transcription factor state
ideas.description: Measure ERK-responsive negative feedback regulators (DUSP6, SPRY2/4) and their protein half-lives across the priming and recovery window, then clamp their levels with inducible knock-in or degron alleles during priming. If AP-1 target memory tracks feedback-regulator dosage rather than AP-1 occupancy, the memory resides in the upstream kinase circuit and not in the transcription factor.

ideas.title: Partner-swap mapping of bZIP heterodimers at memory loci
ideas.description: Use proximity labelling (TurboID or APEX) fused to JUN, FOS, ATF3 and JUNB, plus split-HaloTag complementation, to quantify which heterodimer partners occupy memory enhancers before, during and after priming. A persistent shift in partner composition, such as JUN-ATF3 replacing JUN-FOS, would indicate memory is encoded in a stable heterodimer switch rather than in AP-1 binding alone.

ideas.title: Acetyl-CoA supply gating of memory during priming
ideas.description: Manipulate acetyl-CoA availability during the priming window with ACLY inhibition, acetate supplementation, or a citrate-transporter block, then measure H3K27ac at memory enhancers and re-induction kinetics after washout. A dose-dependent effect on memory strength without changes in AP-1 binding would show that metabolic substrate supply, not AP-1 occupancy, sets how much memory is written.
